A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AugGen work. The complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and can be matched despite extensive layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original face-recognition experiments, real-data scaling comparisons, weighting ablations, and feature-separation analyses in Tables 1–2 and Appendices D–H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and appendix analyses, including the augmentation experiments and comparisons with real-only training.

M1.justification: The architectures, losses, and class-mixing rule remain unchanged. However, Algorithm 1 replaces v1's per-candidate initialization of F with M = {}, while still adding features to F. This changes the written procedure, leaving F uninitialized and clearing accumulated candidate scores; an implemented redesign is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use CASIA-WebFace, WebFace160K, additional WebFace4M data, and the same eight face-recognition benchmarks. v2's explicit mention of eight benchmarks summarizes existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DigiFace1M, RealDigiFace, IDiff-face, DCFace, real-only IR50/IR101 models, and the reproduction control. Table 10 also retains the same four weighting alternatives.

E3.justification: v2's new computational-cost paragraph specifies 1,000 mixes with five samples per class per grid point. Figure 4 in both versions instead specifies 100 combinations with K = 10. The PDFs do not clarify whether this is a revised search protocol or a separate timing configuration. Other stated experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices E–I retain the same sample-count analysis, weighting ablation, generative-metric correlations, feature-separation analysis, and generator-size/training-duration examples. Their relocation introduces no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Mean/std reporting, plotted error bars, and Table 5's seeds remain unchanged. The new statement that repeated training consumed most computation does not specify additional runs or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged. Section 4.2 corrects the WebFace160K finding from beating architectural improvements in 'all cases' to 'most cases': Table 1 retains TinyFace rank-1 scores of 61.60% for AugGen versus 62.59% for real-only IR101. Section 4.1 also newly reports search time below two GPU-days.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the similarity/dissimilarity definitions are retained. Neither version supplies additional theoretical guarantees or proofs; v2's intuitive explanation of mixing weights adds no mathematical result.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit characterization of AugGen as a general formulation of MixUp and CutMix. The central claims about self-contained augmentation, 1–12% improvements, architectural comparisons, real-data savings, and poor generative-metric correlation remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains computational cost through controlled training from scratch and adds expected applicability to autoregressive, flow, other multi-step, and pretrained generators. Future work now also questions how selecting source identities affects augmentation benefits. These are discussion additions without new validation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents grid-search runtime, an RTX 3090 Ti, and a stated workload of 1,000 mixes with five samples per class. Existing appendix hyperparameters, generator-training details, project-page access, and the promised public release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the DeAndres-Tame et al. FRCSyn challenge and Yun et al. CutMix references and drops the direct MixUp/CutMix positioning passage. The remaining related-work discussion and Table 3 survey are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, part of the introduction, and closing discussion are revised, while most prose remains intact. Model subsections become paragraph headings, Class Mixing is renumbered, reproducibility/impact text moves before the gallery, and author information, acknowledgments, and citation style change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout with wrapped figures. Algorithms 1–2 become adjacent, Figure 4's panels are stacked, and tables, plots, and image galleries are extensively resized and repositioned. The same eleven tables and thirteen figures remain.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful motivation and cost information and corrects an overstated architectural comparison. However, Algorithm 1 introduces an initialization error, and the new search workload is not reconciled with Figure 4. These reduce procedural clarity and reproducibility relative to v1, outweighing the limited explanatory gains while the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
